source_caption:
Oscar-worthy performance by Rosamund Pike in Gone Girl.

Pike completely disappears into Amy Dunne, a character who constantly makes you question what’s real and what isn’t. What makes the performance so impressive is how effortlessly she shifts between vulnerability, charm, intelligence, and something much darker without ever losing the character’s control.

David Fincher keeps the audience guessing, but Pike is the reason Amy stays so fascinating. Even when you think you understand her, there’s always another side waiting to come out.

Her performance earned Pike her first Oscar nomination for Best Actress at the 2015 Academy Awards. 

One of the most unforgettable performances of the 2010s.

Do you think Rosamund Pike should have won the Oscar?

source_details.title: Gone Girl
source_details.synopsis: Gone Girl is a 2014 American psychological thriller film directed by David Fincher and written by Gillian Flynn, based on her 2012 novel. It stars Ben Affleck, Rosamund Pike, Neil Patrick Harris, Tyler Perry, and Carrie Coon in her film debut. Affleck plays Nick Dunne, a writing teacher who becomes the prime suspect following the disappearance of his wife, Amy (Pike), in Missouri. Gone Girl premiered as the opening film at the 52nd New York Film Festival on September 26, 2014, and was theatrically released in the US on October 3, 2014, by 20th Century Fox.
